To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Scribble tumor suppressor protein, a member of the LAP protein group, is recruited at cell-cell junctions in an epidermal-cadherin (E-cadherin)-dependent manner in epithelial cells.
hScrib, a tumor suppressor gene involved in the maintenance of epithelial cell polarity, is recruited at cell junctions in an adhesion-dependent manner.
the recruitment of hScreb at epithelial cell-cell junctions is dependent on E-cad.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of hScribble localization at the cell–junctions.
the role of the Scribble complex in epithelial cells and in cancer.
the molecular basis of the junctional recruitment of hSrib, and its role in cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hScrib, as LET-413 and Drosophila scribble, is a junctional protein that is recruited at cell junctions in an epithelial cadherin-dependent manner.
Scribble is not a tumor suppressor gene but that the loss of E-cad and Scribble in the same tumor is associated with poor outcome.
hScrib, like LET-413, is a cell junction protein, but that its recruitment at the junctions depends on E-cad.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
E-cadherins are required to maintain cell–cell adhesion, which in turn is required for the recruitment of hScribe to cell–cell junction.
E-cadherins and LAP proteins cooperate in maintaining epithelial integrity.
hScrib recruitment at the cell–cells junctions is dependent on the presence of E-cad.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hScrib expression is lost in lobular breast cancer and is associated with E-cadherins loss.
the Scrib tumor suppressor protein is a component of the E-cad–catenin–β-catenin complex, and that the loss of Scrib expression in breast cancer is associated with loss of E-cad.

the hScrib protein is recruited at the cell– cell junctions in an epithelial cell-specific manner and is regulated by the E-cad/catenin complex, which is a key player in cell–cell adhesion and epithelial cell polarity.
